mainTopic: The father's right to his daughter's קידושין money, and why the אמה העבריה goes free at both נערות and בגרות
overview: The גמרא is proving that the money from a נערה's קידושין goes to her father. The source is the פסוק about the אמה העבריה who goes free ׳without money׳: no money for this master, but money for another master, the father. The גמרא defends this comparison and answers that the words are already used for another teaching. רבינא's answer is that the extra י in אין is free to teach about the father, and the גמרא shows that this י really is extra. Next it explains why the תורה had to teach both that her קידושין and that her earnings go to her father. Then it returns to the ברייתא and asks why the תורה needs to say she goes free at בגרות if she already went free at נערות. רבה, אביי and מר בר רב אשי each give an answer. The last answer, from מר בר רב אשי, is that the teaching shows that the sale of an אילונית counts at all.

steps.title: The verse only excludes a similar kind of leaving
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק that says ׳no money for this master׳ only rules out money in a ׳leaving׳ that is like the one in the פסוק, where there are two masters.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes a leaving that is like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question about the דרשה. The answer is that the פסוק only speaks about a ׳leaving׳ that matches the case of the אמה העבריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the master who would have received the money is the one she belonged to. So the ׳other master׳ who does get money must also be someone she belongs to and then leaves, and that is her father at קידושין. The דרשה is limited to cases that are built the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: leaving, going out from someone's control

phrases.english: It excludes a leaving that is like it.
phrases.notes: Like it means a case where she leaves one master's control, the way the אמה העבריה does in the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by answering a question raised just before it about the scope of the דרשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the derivation
steps.terutzMaskana: The דרשה compares only similar kinds of ׳leaving׳: from master to freedom, and from father at קידושין.

steps.title: The two kinds of leaving are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two cases are different. The slave girl leaves her master completely, but a girl after קידושין still has not gone to the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this leaving is not like that leaving! There she leaves the master's control completely. Here she is still missing the handing over to the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison from step 1. It says the two cases do not really match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה העבריה who goes free is completely out of her master's control. A girl who got קידושין is still partly under her father until she enters the חופה. So how can one teach about the other?

keyTerms.meaning: handing her over to the wedding canopy

phrases.english: But it is not similar:
this leaving to that leaving.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם נָפְקָא לַהּ מֵרְשׁוּת אָדוֹן לִגְמָרֵי,
phrases.english: There, she leaves the master's control completely,
phrases.notes: There means the slave girl who goes free.

phrases.english: but here, she is still missing the handing over to the חופה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא דָּמְיָא הַאי יְצִיאָה לְהַאי יְצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the slave girl going free and the girl leaving her father at קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full exit cannot be compared to a partial exit, because the girl is still under her father until the חופה.

steps.title: She does leave her father's control for הפרת נדרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that after קידושין she does leave her father's control at least partly, when it comes to cancelling her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least for cancelling vows, she leaves his control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the comparison. Even though she has not fully left her father, she has really left him in one area: הפרת נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before קידושין, the father alone can cancel her vows. After קידושין he cannot do it alone anymore. That is a real ׳leaving׳ of his control, so the comparison still works.

phrases.english: At least regarding cancelling vows
she leaves his control.
phrases.notes: His means the father's.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים מִיהָא נָפְקָא לַהּ מֵרְשׁוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a partial but real similarity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She is still fully under her father until the חופה, so there is no real ׳leaving׳.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her leaving in the area of vows is enough to count as a ׳leaving׳ for the comparison.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about a betrothed girl's vows
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that for a נערה המאורסה, her father and her husband cancel her vows together.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A betrothed young girl, her father and her husband cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove what it said in step 3. The משנה shows the father has lost some control over her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father and the husband must cancel together, then the father can no longer do it alone. This proves she has partly left his control.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned: A betrothed young girl,
her father and her husband cancel her vows.
phrases.notes: They do it together. The father can't cancel alone anymore.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה אָבִיהָ וּבַעְלָהּ מְפִירִין נְדָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 3 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That after קידושין she leaves her father's control regarding vows
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נדרים: אביה ובעלה מפירין נדריה
steps.whatToRemember: The comparison stands. Through קידושין she really leaves her father in one area, vows, so ׳no money for this master, but money for another master׳ can point to the father.

steps.title: The verse is already needed for another teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the words ׳ויצאה חנם׳ are already used in a ברייתא to teach that the אמה העבריה goes free at בגרות and at נערות. So how can we use them for the father's money?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does this ׳she shall go out for nothing׳ come for this? It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: ׳She shall go out for nothing׳: these are the days of adulthood. ׳Without money׳: these are the days of youth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against the whole source. The פסוק seems to be already used up for a different דרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses ׳ויצאה חנם׳ to teach that she goes free when she reaches בגרות, and ׳אין כסף׳ to teach that she goes free at נערות. If both parts of the פסוק are taken, nothing is left to teach that the father gets the money.

keyTerms.meaning: is that what it comes for?
the stage of young girlhood (after the first signs of maturity)

steps.confusionAlert: Here ׳days of נערות׳ and ׳days of בגרות׳ are both times when the אמה העבריה goes free. They are not talking about her father at all.

phrases.english: But this ׳she shall go out for nothing׳,
phrases.notes: שמות 21:11

phrases.english: does it come for this?
It is needed for what was taught,
as it was taught: ׳She shall go out for nothing׳:
these are the days of adulthood;
׳without money׳: these are the days of youth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending the comparison to questioning whether the פסוק is free for this דרשה at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ויצאה חנם אין כסף to prove the father receives קידושין money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already used for one teaching cannot also be used for another, unless there is something extra in it.

steps.title: רבינא: the extra י in אין teaches about the father
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the פסוק could have written אן without a י. The full spelling אין teaches the extra lesson: no money for this master, but there is money for another master, the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: If so, let the פסוק say ׳אן כסף׳. What is ׳אין כסף׳? There is no money for this master, but there is money for another master. And who is he? The father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge of step 5. He finds an extra spelling detail in the פסוק that is free to teach the father's right to the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the ברייתא's lesson, the shorter spelling אן would have been enough. The extra י tells us there is a second lesson. That lesson is that money goes to another master, the father.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא, the one who answers here

steps.whatToRemember: The source that קידושין money of a נערה goes to her father is the extra י in ׳אין כסף׳: no money for this master, but money for another master, the father.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the source for the הלכה that a father receives the money of his daughter's קידושין while she is a נערה.

phrases.english: רבינא said: If so,
let the verse say ׳אן כסף׳.
phrases.notes: That's the same word spelled without the י. It would mean the same thing, so the י is extra.

phrases.english: What is ׳אין כסף׳?
There is no money for this master,
but there is money for another master.
And who is he? The father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא ״אֵן כָּסֶף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra spelling in the verse frees it for a second teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is fully used up by the ברייתא's lesson about נערות and בגרות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra י in אין teaches that the father gets the קידושין money.

steps.title: How do we know an extra letter in אין can be expounded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that the full spelling אין, with a י, can be used to teach a lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that we may expound the word this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבינא's answer from Step 6. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא built a whole law, that the father gets the money, on one extra letter י. The גמרא wants proof that חז״ל really do expound the spelling אין versus אן. It is not attacking רבינא. It is asking for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
We expound (we learn a lesson from the פסוק)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we expound it this way?
phrases.notes: 'This way' means treating the full spelling אין, with a י, as a hint, like רבינא did in Step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the method רבינא used in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A precedent showing that the extra י in אין is expounded.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads זרע אין לה as עיין לה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא expounds the י in ׳אין לה׳ as ׳עיין לה׳, meaning 'examine her'. From this it includes grandchildren and children of flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And she has no child.' This would only teach about her own child. How do we know her grandchild counts too? The פסוק says אין, which we read as עיין, 'examine her'. This would only teach about a child of valid lineage. How do we know a child of flawed lineage counts too? Again the פסוק says אין, read as עיין, 'examine her'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא that clearly learns something from the word אין. This proves that חז״ל do expound this word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the letters of אין as if they said עיין, 'look into her'. That means we look at all her descendants, not just her direct, valid children. Since the ברייתא expounds אין, רבינא may expound it too.
steps.confusionAlert: עיין לה is not a different word written in the תורה. The ברייתא is reading the letters of אין as if they said עיין, because of the extra י.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "And she has no child"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13. It is about a כהן's daughter who married a non-כהן and may eat תרומה again if she has no child.

phrases.english: I would only know this about her own child.
From where do we know her child's child?
The פסוק says: "She has no child"
Read it as: examine her.
phrases.notes: Because of the extra י, the letters of אין are read like עיין, 'look into' her family.

phrases.english: And I would only know this about a child of valid lineage.
From where do we know a child of flawed lineage?
The פסוק says: "She has no child"
Read it as: examine her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by showing a ברייתא that expounds the word אין.
steps.raayaObject: That the full spelling אין is expounded, which supports רבינא's דרשה.

steps.title: The word was already used for grandchildren
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: אין לה was already used to include grandchildren, so how can it also teach about זרע פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used it to teach about her grandchild!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second lesson in the ברייתא. One extra letter should not be used for two separate lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used ׳עיין לה׳ twice: once for grandchildren and once for זרע פסול. Normally, once a word has been used for one lesson, it is 'used up'. So where does the second lesson come from?

keyTerms.meaning: You already used it (to teach something else)

phrases.english: But you already used it to teach about her child's child!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the double use of the same word in the ברייתא from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of ׳עיין לה׳ for זרע פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One extra letter cannot teach two lessons, and it was already used for grandchildren.

steps.title: Grandchildren need no פסוק; the lesson is for זרע פסול
steps.stepSummary: Grandchildren count anyway, because בני בנים הרי הן כבנים. So the פסוק is really only needed for זרע פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: No פסוק was needed for her grandchild, because grandchildren are like children. Where the פסוק was needed was for a child of flawed lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Grandchildren already count by a general rule, so the extra letter is free to teach about זרע פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first question about grandchildren did not really need the פסוק. The rule בני בנים הרי הן כבנים already covers them. So the extra י is used for only one real lesson, זרע פסול, and there is no double use.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא uses אין לה for only one real lesson, זרע פסול. This shows that the extra י in אין is expounded, which backs up רבינא.

phrases.english: For her child's child, no פסוק was needed,
because grandchildren are like children.
Where the פסוק was needed was for a child of flawed lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that one of the two lessons comes from a general rule, so the פסוק is needed for only one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra letter was used twice, for grandchildren and for זרע פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Grandchildren count by the rule בני בנים הרי הן כבנים. The extra letter only teaches about זרע פסול.

steps.title: How did the תנא know to expound the י?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source the תנא of the ברייתא himself had for expounding the extra י in אין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא himself, how did he know to expound it this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes one level deeper. This line sets up the final answer, which explains why the י counts as extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing the ברייתא showed that חז״ל expound אין. But how do we know אין is really an unusual spelling with an extra letter? The גמרא now asks for the basis behind the ברייתא's own method.

phrases.english: And the תנא himself, from where does he know to expound it this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the ברייתא's method, which was used as proof in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the י in אין counts as extra and open to expounding.

steps.title: Other פסוקים spell the same sound without a י
steps.stepSummary: In ׳מאן בלעם׳ and ׳מאן יבמי׳, the same sound is written without a י. So the י in אין is extra and comes to teach a lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It is written 'בלעם refuses' (מאן) and 'my יבם refuses' (מאן), with no י. Here a י is written. Learn from this that it comes to be expounded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה can spell this sound without a י, as other פסוקים show. Since a י was added here, it must be there to teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from comparing spellings. In other places the sound is written as אן, with no י. So the full spelling אין is an extra letter, and an extra letter in the תורה is a hint for a דרשה. This supports both the ברייתא and רבינא.
steps.whatToRemember: The י in אין is extra because other פסוקים write the same sound without it. That extra letter is what lets רבינא learn that the father gets the money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the chain of support for רבינא's דרשה. It shows how the גמרא proves a letter is extra: by comparing spellings in other פסוקים.

phrases.english: They say: It is written "בלעם refuses"
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:14

phrases.english: and "My יבם refuses,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: where no י is written in them.
And here, a י is written in it.
Learn from this that it comes to be expounded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by comparing how the same sound is spelled in other פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Other פסוקים spell the sound without a י, so the י in אין is extra and is meant for a דרשה.

steps.title: Both rules about the father are needed: the betrothal side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both rules had to be written, the father getting the קידושין and the father getting the מעשה ידיה. If only the קידושין rule were written, we would think her earnings stay hers, since she worked for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה had to write both rules. If it had only said the קידושין money goes to the father, we would think that is because she did nothing to earn it. But her earnings, which she worked hard for, we would say are hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תורה needed two separate sources for two rules about a daughter. This step gives the first half of that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that is written could seem to depend on something special about its case. The money for קידושין just comes to her without work, so we might limit the father's right to money she did not toil for. That is why the rule about her earnings had to be written too.

keyTerms.meaning: Her earnings, the work of her hands
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write that her betrothal belongs to her father,
and it was necessary to write that her earnings belong to her father.
For if the Merciful One had written only that her betrothal goes to her father,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא טָרְחָא בְּהוּ,
phrases.english: I would have said that is because she did not toil for it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ דְּקָא טָרְחָא בְּהוּ
phrases.english: but her earnings, which she does toil for,
I would say they are hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the discussion of the extra י to explain why the father's two rights each need their own source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the קידושין rule and the מעשה ידיה rule had to be written. From the קידושין rule alone we would not learn about earnings, because she toils for her earnings.

steps.title: Both rules about the father are needed: the earnings side
steps.stepSummary: If only the earnings rule were written, we would say it is because the father feeds her. Then we would think her קידושין money, which comes from an outside person, stays hers. So both rules are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had only taught us about her earnings, we would say they go to the father because he feeds her. But her קידושין money comes from someone else, so we would say it is hers. That is why both had to be written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation from the other direction and concludes that each rule really needed its own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earnings rule has its own special reason: the father supports her, so it is fair that her work goes to him. The קידושין money comes from the outside world and not from the father's support, so it could not be learned from the earnings rule. The word 'צריכא' closes the argument: both are necessary.
steps.whatToRemember: Each rule has its own special reason. קידושין money comes with no work, and earnings come with the father's support. So neither rule can be learned from the other, and both are written.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about her earnings,
I would say that is because she is fed by him,
but her betrothal money, which comes to her from outside,
I would say it is hers;
so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse side of the explanation and closes it with 'צריכא'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the father's right to her קידושין and his right to her מעשה ידיה need their own source, because each has a reason that does not apply to the other.

steps.title: Returning to the teaching on 'going out for nothing'
steps.stepSummary: With 'גופא' the גמרא goes back to quote the ברייתא again. 'ויצאה חנם' refers to בגרות, and 'אין כסף' refers to נערות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the teaching itself: 'Then she shall go out for nothing' means the days of בגרות (adulthood). 'Without money' means the days of נערות (youth).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a ברייתא it quoted earlier so it can look at it closely. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads two phrases of the פסוק about the אמה העבריה as two separate times when she goes free without paying: at נערות and at בגרות. Quoting it again prepares the ground for asking why both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; a signal that the גמרא is going back to discuss a quoted text
Youth, the stage just after a girl first matures

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself:
"Then she shall go out for nothing": these are the days of adulthood;
phrases.notes: שמות 21:11

phrases.english: "without money": these are the days of youth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא that was quoted earlier, in order to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ויצאה חנם' teaches that she goes free at בגרות, and 'אין כסף' teaches that she goes free at נערות.

steps.title: Why mention adulthood if youth already frees her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the תורה should just write נערות. If she already goes free at נערות, which comes first, there is no need to say she goes free at בגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the תורה write only נערות. Then there would be no need to write בגרות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא, saying one of its two teachings looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נערות comes before בגרות. If she is already free at נערות, she is obviously no longer a servant at בגרות. So the phrase teaching בגרות seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write youth,
and adulthood would not be needed!
phrases.notes: She would already be free at youth, which comes first, so she could not still be a servant at adulthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא נַעֲרוּת, וְלָא בָּעֵי בַּגְרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא just quoted, saying the בגרות teaching is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'ויצאה חנם' to teach freedom at בגרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Going free at נערות, which comes earlier, already covers בגרות, so a separate phrase for בגרות seems wasted.

steps.title: רבה: each phrase explains the other
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that one phrase comes and teaches about the other. Both phrases are needed to show that the תורה really means נערות too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: this one came and taught about that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by showing that the two phrases work together, so neither one is wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה had written only one extra phrase, we would have applied it to בגרות, the easier and more obvious case, and never learned about נערות. The second phrase shows that the first must be teaching something more, which is נערות. So the two phrases together are what teach freedom at נערות.

keyTerms.meaning: This one comes and teaches about that one; one phrase sheds light on the other
An אמורא who gives the answer here

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the תורה needed to tell us she goes free at בגרות. He is saying the second phrase is needed so we can tell that the תורה means נערות.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, with only one phrase we would have read it as בגרות, so having two phrases is what teaches that she goes free already at נערות. אביי rejects this answer in steps 21–22.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
This one came and taught about that one.
phrases.notes: He means each phrase helps us understand the other. Neither one would be clear alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בָּא זֶה וְלִמֵּד עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about why בגרות needed to be written.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the two phrases work together, so the 'extra' phrase is not extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing נערות alone would make בגרות unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without both phrases we could not tell that the תורה means נערות, because one phrase alone would be read as בגרות.

steps.title: רבה's parallel: the tenant and the hired worker
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings a ברייתא about תושב and שכיר as a model for one word teaching about another.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like the case of a tenant and a hired worker. A ברייתא teaches: 'Tenant' means a slave acquired permanently. 'Hired worker' means a slave acquired for a set number of years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה backs up his answer from the last step by pointing to a similar case in a ברייתא. Here the ברייתא only defines its terms; it is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן's תושב and שכיר may not eat תרומה. The ברייתא explains that תושב is an עבד עברי who is owned permanently (until יובל), and שכיר is one owned for six years. רבה wants to show that, like here, the תורה sometimes writes two words so that one explains the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like; introduces a parallel case
Tenant; here, a Hebrew slave owned permanently
Hired worker; here, a Hebrew slave owned for six years
Acquisition for a set number of years

phrases.english: It is just like the case of a tenant and a hired worker.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 22:10, which says these may not eat תרומה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
'Tenant': this is one acquired with a permanent acquisition,
phrases.notes: This is the slave who chose to stay and had his ear pierced. He stays until יובל.

phrases.english: 'Hired worker': this is one acquired for an acquisition of years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's answer in step 17 by bringing a parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: That the תורה may write two terms so that one explains the other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on תושב and שכיר (ויקרא 22:10).

steps.title: Why write 'hired worker' at all?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why 'שכיר' is needed, since a קל וחומר from 'תושב' would teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say 'tenant' and leave out 'hired worker.' I would reason: if a permanently owned slave does not eat תרומה, then a slave owned only for years certainly does not.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is raised: the word 'שכיר' seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanent slave is more closely tied to his master than a six-year slave. So if even he cannot eat his master's תרומה, a קל וחומר tells us the six-year slave cannot either. This is the same kind of question the גמרא asked in step 16 about נערות and בגרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be said (the פסוק could have written only this)
All the more so; a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Let it say 'tenant' and not say 'hired worker,'
and I would say:
if one acquired permanently does not eat,
phrases.notes: He means eating his master's תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: קָנוּי קִנְיַן שָׁנִים לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then one acquired for years, all the more so does not eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the second term in the ברייתא is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra word 'שכיר' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the permanent slave already covers the six-year slave.

steps.title: 'Hired worker' explains what 'tenant' means
steps.stepSummary: Without 'שכיר', we would read 'תושב' as the six-year slave and let the permanent slave eat. 'שכיר' fixes that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that were so, I would have said 'tenant' means the six-year slave, but the permanently owned slave may eat. So 'hired worker' comes and teaches about 'tenant': even though he is owned permanently, he may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'שכיר' is needed to tell us the true meaning of 'תושב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תושב' alone is unclear, so we might have taken it as the six-year slave. Once the פסוק also says 'שכיר', which is clearly the six-year slave, 'תושב' must mean the permanent one. This matches רבה's claim that one phrase teaches about the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Came and taught; one word explains another

steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, 'שכיר' is not extra. It shows that 'תושב' means the permanent slave, so even he may not eat תרומה.

phrases.english: If so, I would have said:
'Tenant': this is one acquired for years.
But one acquired permanently does eat.
So 'hired worker' came and taught about 'tenant,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּנוּי קִנְיַן עוֹלָם – אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: that even though he is acquired permanently, he does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The second word clarifies the meaning of the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תושב' means the six-year slave, so the permanent slave may eat תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שכיר' is the six-year slave, so 'תושב' is the permanent one, and neither may eat.

steps.title: אביי: tenant and hired worker are two different people
steps.stepSummary: אביי questions the parallel. There the two words are about two different people, and the תורה sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר could teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are these alike? There, they are two different people. Even if the תורה had written 'a pierced tenant shall not eat' and then written the other one, the hired worker would just be something that a קל וחומר teaches, and the פסוק sometimes takes the trouble to write out what a קל וחומר teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבה's proof and says the תושב/שכיר case is not like our case. He is setting up a contrast that the גמרא will finish next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תושב and שכיר, writing both is not a problem. They are separate people, so the second word is at worst an extra statement of a קל וחומר, and the תורה does that sometimes. נערות and בגרות are stages of the same girl, so the parallel may not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they alike? Questions a comparison
Pierced; a slave whose ear was pierced
Logic from a lighter case to a stricter one
The פסוק took the trouble to write it out

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He only says it is not a good parallel for נערות and בגרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings in an important rule: the תורה sometimes writes out something that a קל וחומר could have taught.

phrases.english: אביי said to him: Are they comparable?
There, they are two separate people,
phrases.notes: The תושב and the שכיר are two different slaves. A נערה and a בוגרת are the same girl at different ages.

phrases.english: for even if the Merciful One had written
'a pierced tenant shall not eat'
and then written the other one,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה שָׂכִיר מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: the hired worker would be a matter that comes from a קל וחומר,
and a matter that comes from a קל וחומר
the פסוק sometimes takes the trouble and writes it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבה's parallel from steps 18–20 really fits his answer in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the תושב/שכיר ברייתא as a proof for רבה's reading of נערות and בגרות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תושב and שכיר are two different people, and there an extra פסוק can be explained as the תורה writing out a קל וחומר. That is not clearly true for one girl at two stages.

steps.title: Here it is the same girl, so the extra teaching is pointless
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his rejection. With the אמה העבריה there is only one person. Once she goes free at נערות, she is no longer a servant by the time she reaches בגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is one person. Once she has left at נערות, what is she still doing with him at בגרות?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes the point he started in the last step. The תושב and שכיר case does not match our case, because here we are talking about one single girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, תושב and שכיר are two different slaves, so writing both is at worst the תורה spelling out a קל וחומר, which it sometimes does. Here, the same girl reaches נערות first and goes free right then. So a teaching that she goes free at בגרות is not just extra, it has nothing to apply to, and רבה's parallel does not save it.

keyTerms.meaning: the stage of early maturity, when a girl first shows signs of growing up
full adulthood, the stage after נערות

phrases.english: But here,
she is one body;
once she has gone out at youth,
at adulthood, what is she doing with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rejection of רבה's proof, which began in step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה's answer that one phrase teaches about the other, and his proof from the תושב and שכיר ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא deals with two different people. Our case deals with one girl, who has already gone free before בגרות arrives, so there is no point in a separate teaching for בגרות.

steps.title: The teaching is needed for an אילונית who goes straight to adulthood
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new answer. The teaching that she goes free at בגרות is needed for an אילונית, who never goes through נערות. Without it, we might think she never goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: it is only needed for the adulthood of an אילונית. You might have thought: she goes free at נערות, but not at בגרות. So the תורה teaches us that she goes free at בגרות too.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops the earlier approach and offers a fresh reason why the תורה must teach that a girl goes free at בגרות. It is needed for a girl who skips נערות entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אילונית never reaches נערות. She goes straight from being a child to בגרות. If the תורה only said she goes free at נערות, an אילונית would never go free. So the teaching about בגרות covers her.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who never develops the normal signs of maturity and cannot have children
it would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the teaching about בגרות a real, separate job, which answers the problem of why it is needed at all.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
it is needed only
for the adulthood of an aylonit,
phrases.notes: An אילונית never shows the signs of נערות, so she goes straight from child to בוגרת.

phrases.english: it would enter your mind to say:
at youth she goes out,
at adulthood she does not go out;
so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבה's approach, אביי offers his own reason why the teaching about בגרות is needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the teaching to a specific case (an אילונית)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only נערות frees her. An אילונית, who never has נערות, would stay a servant even at בגרות.
steps.terutzMaskana: בגרות also frees her, so an אילונית goes free when she reaches adulthood.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the father's authority should already teach this
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי challenges אביי. The signs of נערות do not free a girl from her father, yet they free her from her master. בגרות does free her from her father, so it should surely free her from her master. Why would we need a פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי objected: isn't it a קל וחומר? The signs of maturity do not take her out of her father's authority, yet they take her out of the master's authority. בגרות does take her out of her father's authority, so surely it takes her out of the master's authority!
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי attacks אביי's answer. He says we would know an אילונית goes free at בגרות from simple logic, without any פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares two levels of authority. The weaker event (סימנים of נערות) does not end the father's authority, yet it still ends the master's. The stronger event (בגרות) does end the father's authority, so it should certainly end the master's. If logic already teaches this, אביי's reason for the פסוק is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: physical signs of maturity that mark נערות
the father's authority over his daughter
the master's authority over his maidservant

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two authorities. The father keeps some control even during נערות (he can still arrange her קידושין), but the master loses control already at נערות.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi objected to this:
But is it not an a fortiori?
Just as the signs,
which do not take her out of the father's authority,
do take her out of the master's authority,
adulthood, which does take her out of the father's authority,
is it not logical
that it takes her out of the master's authority?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְלָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's new answer from step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the פסוק is needed to teach that an אילונית goes free at בגרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר already proves it. סימנים do not end the father's authority yet do end the master's, so בגרות, which does end the father's authority, should surely end the master's. That makes the פסוק unnecessary for this purpose.

steps.title: The teaching shows that selling an אילונית is a real sale
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the teaching is needed to show that an אילונית can be validly sold as an אמה העבריה at all. Without it, we might think the sale only works for a girl who will later show signs of נערות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: The teaching is needed only for the basic sale of an אילונית. You might have thought: a girl who will show signs of נערות can be sold, and the sale works. But a girl who will never show signs of נערות cannot be sold, and her sale is not a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי rejected אביי's answer, so now he offers his own answer for why the teaching is needed. He says it teaches that an אילונית can be sold as a maidservant in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי used the teaching to explain how an אילונית goes free, but מר בר רב אשי showed that a קל וחומר already covers that. So he moves the teaching to an earlier point: the sale itself. Since an אילונית never reaches נערות, we might have thought she does not fit the maidservant laws, and that her sale does not take effect. The teaching shows that her sale does count.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who never develops the physical signs of maturity
The basic sale itself, meaning whether the sale works at all
The physical signs that a girl has become a נערה (young woman)
You might have thought to say. This introduces the mistaken idea that the teaching comes to block.

steps.whatToRemember: מר בר רב אשי: the teaching about בגרות is not about how an אילונית goes free. It teaches that her sale as an אמה העבריה is valid in the first place.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. אביי used the teaching for how she leaves (going free). מר בר רב אשי uses it for how she enters (the sale itself).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא. When a teaching seems to repeat what logic already tells us, the גמרא moves it to a different stage of the case where it adds something new.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
phrases.notes: "Rather" tells you he is dropping אביי's answer from step 23 and offering his own.

phrases.english: It is needed only
for the basic sale of an אילונית,
it might have entered your mind to say:
a girl who will show signs of נערות, it is a sale;
a girl who will not show signs of נערות,
her sale is not a sale.
phrases.notes: The thinking is that she can never reach the stage the maidservant laws talk about, so the sale would not take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְעִיקַּר זְבִינָא דְאַיְלוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's answer in step 24, מר בר רב אשי gives a replacement answer for why the teaching is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the teaching to a different stage (the validity of the sale instead of going free)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought that only a girl who will later show signs of נערות can be sold, so the sale of an אילונית would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching shows that an אילונית can be validly sold as an אמה העבריה.
